title: Fort William falls; Europeans are confined
detail: After the fort fell, some Europeans were confined overnight in a cell within Fort William. The surviving accounts do not independently establish the number confined or the number who died.

title: The prisoners are released
detail: Holwell's account dates the opening of the cell and the release of surviving prisoners to the following morning; this detail is presented as his testimony.

title: Clive frames British action as retribution
detail: In a 30 July 1757 letter to the Mughal emperor, Robert Clive described the deaths as ordered by Siraj-ud-Daulah and presented British military action as revenge for the injuries. This is Clive's partisan justification, not independent confirmation of the alleged order.

title: Holwell erects a memorial
detail: Holwell's memorial inscription blamed Siraj for the deaths and described British revenge as deserved, a change from the qualification in Holwell's earlier narrative, as Mukherjee argues.
